mainTopic: A child's obligation in ראייה, and the debate between בית שמאי and בית הלל over the minimum values of the ראייה and חגיגה offerings
overview: The גמרא asks how a small child even reached ירושלים, and אביי explains that his mother brought him, since she comes anyway for the מצוה of שמחה. רבי tries to prove בית הלל's age rule from חנה, who kept שמואל home until he was weaned. His father rejects the proof: חנה stayed home only to protect a delicate child. רבי שמעון then asks about a lame or blind child who might heal. אביי rules that a child is trained only where an adult in the same condition would be obligated. The גמרא then turns to the minimum value of the ראייה and חגיגה offerings, where בית שמאי and בית הלל each give two reasons and answer each other's arguments. The debate comes down to whether the עולות brought at סיני were עולות ראייה or the עולת תמיד. אביי lists other תנאים on each side, and the גמרא begins tracing their sources, a discussion that continues on the next amud.

steps.title: Who brought the child to Jerusalem?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks how a young child got as far as ירושלים in the first place.
steps.simpleTranslation: Up to here, to ירושלים, who brought him?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is asking a practical question about the child's age rule. The rule only talks about the walk from ירושלים to הר הבית, so who got the child to ירושלים?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The age test for a child is about the short climb from ירושלים up to הר הבית. That leaves a gap: a child this young could not travel the whole long road to ירושלים on his own. Someone must have brought him, and the גמרא wants to know who, and why that person could not also bring him up to the הר הבית.

keyTerms.meaning: Up to here (to ירושלים)
Who brought him?

phrases.english: Up to here, who brought him?
phrases.notes: "Here" means ירושלים. The child's test only starts from ירושלים, so how did he get that far?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Picks up the earlier definition of a קטן, which is measured by the walk from ירושלים to הר הבית.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who brought the child as far as ירושלים, and why does that not make him obligated for the rest of the way?

steps.title: His mother brought him; from Jerusalem on, it depends on the child
steps.stepSummary: אביי answers that the mother brought him to ירושלים. From there on, whether the child is obligated depends on whether he can walk up holding his father's hand.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Up to here, since his mother is obligated in שמחה, his mother brought him. From here on, if he can go up holding his father's hand from ירושלים to הר הבית, he is obligated. If not, he is exempt.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי explains that the mother, who comes anyway for the מצוה of שמחה, brought the child to ירושלים. The child's own obligation is judged only from ירושלים up to הר הבית.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Women are not obligated in the מצוה of appearing (ראייה), but they are obligated in שמחה on the festival. So the mother travels to ירושלים anyway and naturally brings her small child along. The child's own obligation is not measured by that long trip. It is measured only by the last stretch: can he walk up to הר הבית holding his father's hand?

keyTerms.meaning: The מצוה of rejoicing on the festival, which also applies to women
His mother
To hold his father's hand (the test of בית הלל)
The Temple Mount
Exempt

steps.whatToRemember: The mother brings the child to ירושלים because of her own מצוה of שמחה. The child's obligation is judged only by the walk from ירושלים to הר הבית.

phrases.english: Abaye said to him:
Up to here, since his mother is obligated in rejoicing,
his mother brought him.
From here onward,

phrases.aramaic: אִם יָכוֹל לַעֲלוֹת וְלֶאֱחוֹז בְּיָדוֹ שֶׁל אָבִיו
phrases.english: if he is able to go up holding his father's hand
from Jerusalem to the Temple Mount, he is obligated,
and if not, he is exempt.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 1.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The mother, who is obligated in שמחה, brought him to ירושלים. The child's own obligation is measured only from ירושלים to הר הבית.

steps.title: רבי's proof from חנה and שמואל
steps.stepSummary: רבי argues for בית הלל: חנה did not bring שמואל until he was weaned, even though he could already ride on his father's shoulders. That fits בית הלל, not בית שמאי.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי answered on behalf of בית הלל: According to בית שמאי, how do you explain the verse "But חנה did not go up, for she said to her husband: Until the child is weaned, and then I will bring him"? שמואל was already able to ride on his father's shoulders!
steps.whatsHappening: רבי brings a proof for בית הלל from a פסוק. חנה kept שמואל home even though he could already ride on his father's shoulders.
steps.deeperAnalysis: According to בית שמאי, a child who can ride on his father's shoulders is already obligated. Even before he was weaned, שמואל could already be carried that way, yet חנה waited until he was weaned before bringing him. So that kind of child was apparently not yet obligated, which supports בית הלל's later age: a child who can walk holding his father's hand.

keyTerms.meaning: Answered or argued back
In place of, on behalf of
Will be weaned
To ride on his shoulders (the test of בית שמאי)

phrases.english: Rabbi responded on behalf of Beit Hillel:
According to the words of Beit Shammai,
"But Hannah did not go up,
for she said to her husband:
Until the child is weaned, and then I will bring him"?
But Samuel was able to ride
on his father's shoulders!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from explaining the rule to testing the debate between בית שמאי and בית הלל against a פסוק.
steps.raayaObject: That a child who can only ride on his father's shoulders is not yet obligated, which supports בית הלל.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The פסוק in שמואל א 1:22 about חנה waiting until שמואל was weaned.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית שמאי's age test (riding on the father's shoulders)
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: שמואל already passed בית שמאי's test, yet he was not brought up, so that test must be too early.

steps.title: His father rejects the proof: חנה stayed home to protect a delicate child
steps.stepSummary: רבי's father points out that חנה herself was obligated in שמחה and still stayed home. So the story is not about the age of obligation; she stayed home to protect a delicate child from a hard trip.
steps.simpleTranslation: His father said to him: By your reasoning, you should also ask: wasn't חנה herself obligated in שמחה? Rather, חנה saw that שמואל needed extra care, and she worried about him becoming weak from the journey.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי's father knocks down the proof. Since חנה also skipped her own מצוה, the story must be about a special situation, not the general age rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the story were teaching the law, it would also mean חנה was allowed to skip her own מצוה of שמחה, which cannot be the normal rule. So her choice was personal: שמואל was delicate, and the trip would have weakened him. Since she could not bring him, she stayed home with him, and nothing can be learned about the age of obligation.

keyTerms.meaning: And according to your own reasoning
You should also find this difficult
Delicateness, needing pampering
Weakness from the journey

steps.whatToRemember: The story of חנה is not a proof about the age of obligation. It was a special case of a delicate child, so the debate between בית שמאי and בית הלל stays open.
steps.confusionAlert: Do not think the father is rejecting בית הלל. He only shows that the story of חנה cannot prove either side.

phrases.english: His father said to him:
And according to your reasoning, it should be difficult for you:

phrases.aramaic: חַנָּה גּוּפַהּ מִי לָא מִיחַיְּיבָא בְּשִׂמְחָה?
phrases.english: Was Hannah herself not obligated in rejoicing?
Rather, Hannah saw extra delicateness
in Samuel,
and she was concerned about Samuel
becoming weak from the journey.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ אֲבוּהּ: וּלְטַעְמָיךְ, תִּיקְשֵׁי לָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects רבי's proof in step 3.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: The whole proof from the story of חנה
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: חנה also skipped her own obligation of שמחה, so her staying home reflects a special concern for a delicate child, not a general age rule.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The story of חנה is not proof for בית הלל against בית שמאי.

steps.title: רבי שמעון asks about a lame or blind child
steps.stepSummary: רבי שמעון asks what the law is for a lame child according to בית שמאי, and for a blind child according to both בית שמאי and בית הלל.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי שמעון asked: What is the law for a lame child according to בית שמאי, and for a blind child according to both of them?
steps.whatsHappening: רבי שמעון raises a question about children who are lame or blind. Must they be brought up to ירושלים for the חג?
steps.deeperAnalysis: By בית שמאי, a child who can ride on his father's shoulders must be brought, and a lame child can still ride. By both opinions, a child who can hold his father's hand and walk must be brought, and a blind child can still do that. But an adult who is lame or blind is exempt, so it is unclear what to do with such a child.

keyTerms.meaning: He asked a question (an open question, not an attack)
A child who is not yet בר מצוה
Lame; unable to walk properly
Blind

steps.confusionAlert: Why does the lame child count only 'according to בית שמאי'? Only בית שמאי obligate a child who is carried on his father's shoulders. בית הלל require the child to walk holding his father's hand, which a lame child cannot do anyway.

phrases.english: Rabbi Shimon asked:
A lame child, according to the words of Beit Shammai,
phrases.notes: By בית שמאי, a child who can ride on his father's shoulders must come, and a lame child can still ride.

phrases.english: and a blind child, according to the words of both of them,
what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Builds on the age rules for bringing a child (shoulders or holding a hand), now applied to a disabled child.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Must a lame or blind child, who could physically be brought up, be trained in the מצוה of ראייה?

steps.title: What case is the question about?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks which case רבי שמעון means. It rejects the idea that he means a child who can never heal, since even an adult like that is exempt.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the case? If you say it is a lame child who cannot heal and a blind child who cannot gain sight, that is obvious! If an adult like that is exempt, why ask about a child?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא pins down what exact case רבי שמעון is asking about. It first tests one possibility and throws it out as too obvious to need asking.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If the child can never heal, he will never be obligated even as an adult. Then there is clearly nothing to train him for. So the question cannot be about that case, and the גמרא is getting ready to give the real case.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the case? What are the exact circumstances?
If you say (introduces a possibility that will be rejected)
Now (that is, if even this is true...)
Is it even a question?

phrases.english: What is the case?
If you say it is a lame child who cannot be healed,
phrases.notes: לְהִתְפַּשֵּׁט literally means 'to stretch out.' Here it means the leg cannot get better.

phrases.english: and a blind child whose eyes cannot open,
now, if an adult in that state is exempt,
is there any question about a child?!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Clarifies the case of the question in step 5 by rejecting the obvious reading.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which kind of lame or blind child is רבי שמעון asking about?

steps.title: The question is about a child who may heal
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that the question is about a lame or blind child who could still recover.
steps.simpleTranslation: No, the question is needed for a lame child who can heal and a blind child whose eyes can open. What is the law?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the real case behind רבי שמעון's question: a child whose condition could still improve.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This child may one day be fully obligated, so maybe we should train him now for that future. On the other hand, right now he is like an adult who is exempt. That is the real doubt.

keyTerms.meaning: It is not needed (for that case); the question is really about this case
To straighten out; here, for the leg to heal
To open up; here, for the eyes to gain sight

phrases.english: No, it is needed
for a lame child who can be healed,
and a blind child whose eyes can open;
what is the law?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the clarifying question of step 6 by giving the real case.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The question is about a child who could heal: must we train him now, since he may later be obligated?

steps.title: אביי's rule for training children
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that we train a child only where an adult in the same condition would be obligated from the Torah. Where such an adult is exempt, the child is exempt too.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Wherever an adult is obligated from the Torah, we also train a child, from דרבנן. Wherever an adult is exempt from the Torah, a child is also exempt from דרבנן.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי answers רבי שמעון's question with a general rule for חינוך. He compares the child to an adult in the same condition right now.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Training a child is a דרבנן that follows the Torah's rule for adults. We look at the child's condition today, not what might happen later. An adult who is lame or blind now is exempt, so the child who might heal is exempt too.

keyTerms.meaning: We train (a child in מצוות)
From the Torah
From the Rabbis
Wherever; in any case where

steps.whatToRemember: חינוך follows the adult rule: train a child only where an adult in his current condition would be obligated. A lame or blind child is exempt even if he might heal later.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general rule about חינוך that reaches beyond ראייה: the child's training obligation mirrors the adult's Torah obligation.

phrases.english: Abaye said:
Wherever an adult is obligated by Torah law,
we also train a child by rabbinic law;
wherever an adult is exempt by Torah law,
a child is also exempt by rabbinic law.
phrases.notes: Applied here: a lame or blind adult is exempt, so this child is exempt too, even if he might heal.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: כֹּל הֵיכָא דְּגָדוֹל מִיחַיַּיב מִדְּאוֹרָיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the question that was clarified in step 7.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A child is trained only where an adult in the same condition is obligated. Since a lame or blind adult is exempt, the child is exempt.

steps.title: Quoting the משנה on the value of the offering
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens a new topic by quoting the משנה: בית שמאי say the ראייה offering must be worth at least two silver coins.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית שמאי say: The ראייה offering must be worth at least two silver coins, and so on.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next part of the משנה and quotes its opening words. This sets up the discussion that follows.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'and so on' means the rest of the משנה line is assumed: the חגיגה must be worth at least one מעה כסף, and בית הלל reverse the amounts. The גמרא will now discuss the reasoning behind these minimum values.

keyTerms.meaning: The עולה brought when appearing at the בית המקדש on a רגל
Two silver coins (two מעה כסף)
And so on; the rest of the quote is assumed

phrases.english: Beit Shammai say:
The appearance offering must be worth two silver coins, etc.
phrases.notes: The rest of the משנה: the חגיגה is worth one מעה כסף, and בית הלל switch the two amounts.

steps.triggerLanguage: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי אוֹמְרִים: הָרְאִיָּיה שְׁתֵּי כֶּסֶף
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new topic after the training discussion ended.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: By בית שמאי, the ראייה offering must be worth at least two silver coins.

steps.title: בית שמאי's view and their two reasons
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא records that בית שמאי require the ראייה to be worth two silver coins and the חגיגה one מעה. Their first reason is that the ראייה goes entirely to the מזבח. Their second is that on עצרת the Torah commands more עולות than שלמים.
steps.simpleTranslation: The Rabbis taught: בית שמאי say the ראייה offering must be worth two silver coins and the חגיגה offering one silver מעה. This is because the ראייה goes up entirely to ה׳, which is not so with the חגיגה. Also, we find that on עצרת the verse commands more burnt-offerings than peace-offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that explains the reasons behind בית שמאי's opinion in the משנה we just quoted.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי give the ראייה the higher minimum value. Their first reason is about holiness: an עולה is burned completely for ה׳, but most of a שלמים is eaten by people. Their second reason is a pattern in the Torah: on עצרת there are more עולות than שלמים, which shows the עולה is more important.

keyTerms.meaning: The Rabbis taught; this introduces a ברייתא
One silver מעה, a small silver coin
It goes up entirely to ה׳; the whole animal is burned on the מזבח
שבועות
Peace-offerings, which are mostly eaten by people

phrases.english: The Rabbis taught: Beit Shammai say:
The appearance offering must be worth two silver coins,
phrases.notes: "Two silver" means two silver מעה coins.

phrases.english: and the Festival offering one silver ma'ah.
For the appearance offering goes up entirely to the Most High,
which is not so with the Festival offering,
And furthermore: we find regarding Atzeret
that the verse increased with them
burnt-offerings more than peace-offerings.
phrases.notes: On שבועות the Torah lists ten animals as עולות and only two sheep as שלמים.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reasoning behind בית שמאי's opinion in the משנה quoted in step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי: ראייה is at least two silver coins and חגיגה at least one מעה, because the עולה goes fully to ה׳ and because עצרת has more עולות.

steps.title: בית הלל's view and their two reasons
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל reverse the amounts: the ראייה is one מעה and the חגיגה two silver coins. Their first reason is that the חגיגה existed before מתן תורה. Their second is that the נשיאים brought more שלמים than עולות.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל say the ראייה must be worth one silver מעה and the חגיגה two silver coins. This is because the חגיגה existed before ה׳ spoke at סיני, which is not so with the ראייה. Also, we find that with the נשיאים the verse lists more peace-offerings than burnt-offerings.
steps.whatsHappening: The same ברייתא continues and gives בית הלל's opposite opinion, with two reasons of their own.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל give the חגיגה the higher value. First, it is older: the חגיגה was already brought before the Torah was given, so it has a kind of seniority. Second, they point to the Torah's own pattern with the נשיאים, who brought more שלמים than עולות.

keyTerms.meaning: Before ה׳'s speech, meaning before מתן תורה at סיני
The tribal leaders who brought offerings when the משכן was dedicated
It exists, or it already existed

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel say:
The appearance offering, one silver ma'ah,
and the Festival offering, two silver coins.
For the Festival offering existed before the Speech,
phrases.notes: "The Speech" means ה׳ giving the Torah at סיני.

phrases.english: which is not so with the appearance offering.
And furthermore: we find regarding the princes
that the verse increased with them
peace-offerings more than burnt-offerings.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposite view and reasons, set side by side with step 10.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית הלל: ראייה is at least one מעה and חגיגה at least two silver coins, because the חגיגה existed before מתן תורה and because the נשיאים brought more שלמים.

steps.title: Why don't בית הלל accept בית שמאי's reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks why בית הלל are not convinced by בית שמאי's two arguments.
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית הלל, what is their reason for not agreeing with בית שמאי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking how בית הלל would answer בית שמאי's two reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both sides have given reasons that sound good. The גמרא now wants to see how בית הלל would answer each of בית שמאי's points.

keyTerms.meaning: What is the reason?
They do not say like; they do not agree with

phrases.english: And Beit Hillel, what is the reason
that they do not say like Beit Shammai?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמְרִי כְּבֵית שַׁמַּאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns from stating the opinions to testing them against each other.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How בית הלל answer each of בית שמאי's two arguments.

steps.title: The חגיגה is better because it is eaten twice
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer the first argument: the opposite is true. The חגיגה is better because it has two eatings, on the מזבח and by people.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said the ראייה is better because it goes up entirely to ה׳. On the contrary, the חגיגה is better, because it has two eatings.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית הלל's answer to בית שמאי's first reason and flips it around.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית שמאי treated going entirely to the מזבח as the highest level. בית הלל say it is better for an offering to be eaten both by the מזבח and by its owners, which is two eatings instead of one. So by this measure the חגיגה is the more important offering.

keyTerms.meaning: Better, superior
On the contrary
Two eatings

phrases.english: That which you said: the appearance offering is better
because it goes up entirely to the Most High,
on the contrary: the Festival offering is better
because it has two eatings.
phrases.notes: Part is "eaten" by the fire on the מזבח and the rest is eaten by people.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first half of the answer to the question in step 12.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Two eatings make the חגיגה more important than an offering that is fully burned.

steps.title: Learn a private offering from a private offering
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל answer the second argument: you cannot learn from עצרת, because those are communal offerings. A private offering should be compared to another private offering, like those of the נשיאים.
steps.simpleTranslation: And you said we should learn from עצרת. But we compare a private offering to a private offering. We do not compare a private offering to a communal offering.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית הלל's answer to בית שמאי's second reason, the proof from עצרת.
steps.deeperAnalysis: ראייה and חגיגה are brought by each person for himself. The עצרת offerings are brought for the whole community, so they are not a good model. The נשיאים each brought their own offering, so בית הלל's source is the better comparison.

keyTerms.meaning: Let us learn or derive
We compare and learn one case from another
An offering brought by an individual
An offering brought for the whole community

steps.whatToRemember: בית הלל answer both of בית שמאי's points. Two eatings beat being fully burned, and a private offering must be learned from the נשיאים (private), not from עצרת (communal).

phrases.english: And that which you said: let us learn from Atzeret
we derive an individual's offering from an individual's offering,
phrases.notes: He means the נשיאים, since each one brought his own offering.

phrases.aramaic: וְאֵין דָּנִין קׇרְבַּן יָחִיד מִקׇּרְבַּן צִבּוּר.
phrases.english: and we do not derive an individual's offering from a communal offering.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes בית הלל's answer by dealing with the second argument.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The עצרת offerings are communal, so they cannot teach about private offerings. The private offerings of the נשיאים are the right model.

steps.title: Why don't בית שמאי accept בית הלל's reasons?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks the reverse question: why are בית שמאי not convinced by בית הלל's arguments?
steps.simpleTranslation: And בית שמאי, what is their reason for not agreeing with בית הלל?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא sets up the next move by asking how בית שמאי would answer בית הלל's reasons.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Now that בית הלל have answered בית שמאי, the גמרא turns the question around. This keeps the discussion fair to both sides.

keyTerms.meaning: And בית שמאי; this opens the reverse question

phrases.english: And Beit Shammai, what is the reason
that they do not say like Beit Hillel?

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית שַׁמַּאי, מַאי טַעְמָא לָא אָמְרִי כְּבֵית הִלֵּל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Mirrors the question of step 12, now asked from the other side.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: How בית שמאי answer בית הלל's arguments.

steps.title: The ראייה also existed before סיני
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer בית הלל's first argument: the ראייה also existed before מתן תורה, so the חגיגה has no special seniority.
steps.simpleTranslation: You said the חגיגה is better because it existed before ה׳ spoke at סיני. But the ראייה also existed before ה׳ spoke.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives בית שמאי's answer to בית הלל's first reason.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל claimed that only the חגיגה was brought before מתן תורה. בית שמאי reply that עולות were brought then too, so both offerings are equally old. That takes away בית הלל's advantage.

keyTerms.meaning: Also, too

steps.confusionAlert: בית שמאי are not saying the ראייה is older than the חגיגה. They are only saying the two are equal in age, which cancels בית הלל's reason.

phrases.english: That which you said: the Festival offering is better
because it existed before the Speech,
the appearance offering also existed before the Speech.
phrases.notes: בית שמאי hold that עולות were also brought at סיני before the Torah was given.

steps.triggerLanguage: דְּקָאָמְרַתְּ: חֲגִיגָה עֲדִיפָא — דְּיֶשְׁנָהּ לִפְנֵי הַדִּיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the first part of the answer to the question in step 15.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both the ראייה and the חגיגה existed before מתן תורה, so age gives the חגיגה no advantage.

steps.title: בית שמאי reject learning from the נשיאים
steps.stepSummary: בית שמאי answer בית הלל's second argument: you cannot learn a permanent law from the offerings of the נשיאים, which were a one-time event.
steps.simpleTranslation: And as for your point that we should learn from the נשיאים: we learn a permanent law from another permanent law, not from something that happened only once.
steps.whatsHappening: בית שמאי answer the second argument of בית הלל, the comparison to the offerings of the נשיאים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל said a private offering should be learned from another private offering, like those of the נשיאים. בית שמאי reply that the חגיגה and ראייה apply in every generation, while the offerings of the נשיאים were brought only once, at the חנוכת המשכן. So the better comparison is still עצרת, which also applies in every generation.

keyTerms.meaning: The tribal leaders who brought offerings when the משכן was dedicated
We learn one law from another
Applies in all generations; a permanent law

steps.whatToRemember: Each side picks a different comparison: בית הלל compare private to private (the נשיאים), and בית שמאי compare permanent to permanent (עצרת).

phrases.english: And as for what you said: let us learn from the princes —
phrases.notes: This is בית שמאי speaking to בית הלל, answering their second reason from Step 11, the offerings of the נשיאים.

phrases.english: we learn a matter that applies for all generations
from a matter that applies for all generations,
but we do not learn a matter that applies for all generations
from a matter that does not apply for all generations.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Completes בית שמאי's reply. Step 16 answered the first argument, and this step answers the second.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why בית שמאי are not convinced by the comparison to the נשיאים
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: A permanent law is learned only from another permanent law, and the offerings of the נשיאים were a one-time event.

steps.title: The same פסוק mentions עולות before מתן תורה
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges בית הלל: if the חגיגה existed before מתן תורה because of the שלמים in the פסוק, the ראייה should count too, since the same פסוק mentions עולות.
steps.simpleTranslation: And according to בית הלל, why is the חגיגה special because it existed before מתן תורה, as it says 'they sacrificed שלמים'? The ראייה is there too, because it says 'they offered עולות'!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks בית הלל's claim that the חגיגה is older than the ראייה. It backs up בית שמאי's point from Step 16 with a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: בית הלל argued that the חגיגה (a שלמים) comes first because שלמים were brought before מתן תורה. But the very same פסוק also mentions עולות, and the ראייה is an עולה. So how can בית הלל say the חגיגה has seniority?

keyTerms.meaning: What is different? Why treat this case differently?
Before the Divine speech, meaning before מתן תורה
Peace-offerings. The חגיגה is this kind of offering
Burnt-offerings. The ראייה is this kind of offering

phrases.english: And according to Beit Hillel, what is different about the Festival peace-offering
that it existed before the Divine speech,
phrases.notes: "The speech" means God giving the תורה at סיני.

phrases.english: as it is written: "And they sacrificed peace-offerings",
the appearance-offering also existed, for isn't it written: "And they offered up burnt-offerings"!
phrases.notes: These words come from the same פסוק, right before the שלמים.

steps.triggerLanguage: וּבֵית הִלֵּל, מַאי שְׁנָא חֲגִיגָה דְּיֶשְׁנָהּ לִפְנֵי הַדִּיבּוּר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Turns בית שמאי's point from Step 16 into a direct challenge to בית הלל.
steps.kashyaTarget: בית הלל's claim that the חגיגה is older than the ראייה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק that shows שלמים before מתן תורה also shows עולות, so the ראייה should be just as old.

steps.title: The עולות at סיני were the עולת תמיד
steps.stepSummary: בית הלל hold that the עולות brought at סיני were the עולת תמיד, a communal offering. בית שמאי hold they were עולות ראייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: בית הלל hold that the עולה Israel brought in the desert was the עולת תמיד. בית שמאי hold it was the עולת ראייה.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge by showing that the two sides read the עולות in the פסוק differently.
steps.deeperAnalysis: If those עולות were the עולת תמיד, they were not a ראייה at all. Then only the שלמים (the חגיגה) existed before מתן תורה, and בית הלל's argument stands. בית שמאי read them as עולות ראייה, which is why they said the ראייה was there too.

keyTerms.meaning: The daily burnt-offering, brought for the whole community
The burnt-offering a person brings when coming to the בית המקדש on a festival
They hold; this is their view
In the desert, meaning at הר סיני

steps.whyThisMatters: The whole argument about which offering is older depends on how each side reads one פסוק.

phrases.english: Beit Hillel hold:
the burnt-offering that the Jewish people sacrificed in the desert —
was the daily burnt-offering.
And Beit Shammai hold:
the burnt-offering that the Jewish people sacrificed in the desert —
was a burnt-offering of appearance.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 18.
steps.terutzResolutionType: The two sides read the פסוק differently
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The עולות in the פסוק were ראייה offerings, so the ראייה existed before מתן תורה
steps.terutzMaskana: According to בית הלל they were the עולת תמיד, so only the חגיגה existed before מתן תורה

steps.title: אביי lists who holds each view
steps.stepSummary: אביי says בית שמאי, רבי אלעזר and רבי ישמעאל hold the עולה in the desert was a ראייה. בית הלל, רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי hold it was a תמיד.
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: בית שמאי, רבי אלעזר and רבי ישמעאל all hold the עולה brought in the desert was an עולת ראייה. בית הלל, רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי all hold it was an עולת תמיד.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי shows that this argument about the עולה in the desert is not only between בית שמאי and בית הלל. Other תנאים are split the same way.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי groups the תנאים into two camps based on the question just raised. This connects the debate here to a wider argument found elsewhere among the תנאים.

keyTerms.meaning: All of them
They hold; this is their opinion
An אמורא who often organizes opinions into groups

steps.whatToRemember: There are two camps. The עולה at סיני was a ראייה according to בית שמאי, רבי אלעזר and רבי ישמעאל. It was a תמיד according to בית הלל, רבי עקיבא and רבי יוסי הגלילי.

phrases.english: Abaye said:

phrases.aramaic: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל,
phrases.english: Beit Shammai, Rabbi Elazar, and Rabbi Yishmael,
all of them hold:
the burnt-offering that the Jewish people sacrificed in the desert —
was a burnt-offering of appearance.

phrases.aramaic: וּבֵית הִלֵּל, וְרַבִּי עֲקִיבָא, וְרַבִּי יוֹסֵי הַגְּלִילִי,
phrases.english: And Beit Hillel, Rabbi Akiva, and Rabbi Yosei HaGelili,
all of them hold:
the burnt-offering that the Jewish people sacrificed in the desert —
was a daily burnt-offering.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: בֵּית שַׁמַּאי, וְרַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר, וְרַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל, כּוּלְּהוּ סְבִירָא לְהוּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Takes the argument from Step 19 and lists the other תנאים on each side.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Two groups of תנאים argue whether the עולה at סיני was an עולת ראייה or an עולת תמיד.

steps.title: The source for בית שמאי was already given
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins showing the sources for אביי's list. For בית שמאי, the source is the earlier discussion: they hold the עולות at סיני were עולות ראייה.
steps.simpleTranslation: Where do we see that בית שמאי hold this? From what we already said.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts going through אביי's list one name at a time. It says the source for בית שמאי was already explained earlier.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אביי claimed in step 20 that בית שמאי hold the desert עולה was a ראייה. The גמרא does not need a new source, because steps 18 and 19 already showed it. בית שמאי read the עולות at סיני as עולות ראייה.

keyTerms.meaning: That which we said, pointing back to an earlier discussion
The burnt offering brought when coming to the בית המקדש on a festival

phrases.english: Beit Shammai:
is what we already said.
phrases.notes: This points back to step 19, where בית שמאי said the עולות brought at סיני were עולות ראייה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Begins tracing the sources for each name in אביי's list from step 20.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: בית שמאי's view that the desert עולה was a ראייה comes from the earlier discussion (step 19).

steps.title: Opening the ברייתא that is the source for רבי ישמעאל
steps.stepSummary: For רבי ישמעאל, the גמרא quotes a ברייתא. It begins with his statement that general rules were said at סיני. The rest of the ברייתא continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: And רבי ישמעאל? As a ברייתא teaches: רבי ישמעאל says, general rules were said at סיני,
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is starting to bring a ברייתא to show where רבי ישמעאל's opinion comes from. This line only sets things up, and the proof itself comes in the lines that follow.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי ישמעאל's opening principle is that at סיני, משה received the מצוות only in a general way. The ברייתא will build from this to show how רבי ישמעאל understands the offerings in the desert. That will connect him to the ראייה side of אביי's list.

keyTerms.meaning: As it was taught in a ברייתא
General rules, the broad outlines of the מצוות
Were said at הר סיני

steps.confusionAlert: This is not the end of the proof. The ברייתא keeps going, so do not try to see the connection to the ראייה from these words alone.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yishmael: as it is taught in a baraita,
Rabbi Yishmael says:
general rules were said at Sinai,

steps.triggerLanguage: רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל דְּתַנְיָא רַבִּי יִשְׁמָעֵאל אוֹמֵר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from בית שמאי to רבי ישמעאל, another name on אביי's ראייה list.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's claim that רבי ישמעאל holds the desert עולה was a ראייה.
steps.raayaSupportSource: A ברייתא of רבי ישמעאל, opening with 'כללות נאמרו בסיני'. It continues on the next amud.
